about.en: The inner reap sends them backwards on the same side you are about to attack from outside. O-soto-gake takes the leg they have just planted to stop themselves.

en: Take your right grips and reap their right foot inwards with your right sole.
Feel them plant that foot again and load their weight onto it.
Step your left foot forward beside their right foot, close, and keep your chest tight.
Swing your right leg past their right side and hook your calf behind their right leg.
Drive forward and down over the hook with both hands.
They fall straight backwards; keep hold of the sleeve and stay over them.

receiving.en: Replacing the foot after the inner reap feels like the safe thing to do and it loads the leg they are about to attack. Their calf hooks behind that same leg from the outside, their hands drive down and forward, and you go straight backwards over a leg that cannot move. There is no time to step. Keep your chin on your chest, do not post an arm behind you, and slap with your free arm as your back meets the mat.

viNotes.en: The two attacks are the same side and the same leg, so nothing has to be found twice: your foot already knows where their leg is when you change from a reap to a hook. Step your other foot in close before you hook, because the hook needs your chest tight to theirs to be worth anything. Their weight settling back onto the foot is felt in your lapel hand.

cue.en: The inside flick sends them back, and the leg they plant is hooked out.
